newsitem.title: UK: Irish prisoner bows out of poll fight - Sinn Fein.
newsitem.headline: Irish prisoner bows out of poll fight - Sinn Fein.

text.p: Roisin McAliskey, a pregnant Irish prisoner in England wanted in Germany for questioning about an IRA bombing, abandoned plans on Sunday to stand in Britain's election on May 1.

The Irish Republican Army's Sinn Fein political arm said it had learned that the 25-year-old, who had threatened to run as an independent to put pressure on Britain to release her before the birth of her child, would not do so.
Sinn Fein spokesman Francis Molloy said in a statement that he welcomed "the decision from the McAliskey family that Roisin will not be contesting the forthcoming election".

Bernadette McAliskey, the prisoner's mother, who announced the candidature last week, could not be contacted for comment. She has accused Britain of harshly treating her eight months-pregnant daughter and said Roisin would contest the Mid-Ulster constituency unless she was released.
Bernadette McAliskey was a nationalist parliamentarian for the constituency in 1969-74.

She had appealed to the province's main Catholic nationalist Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) and Sinn Fein to withdraw from the contest so that Roisin might win Catholic votes en bloc and unseat the Protestant "Unionist" incumbent.
The SDLP rejected the plea, saying the elections for Northern Ireland's 18 seats in the British parliament came at a crucial time for the region's floundering peace process.
Sinn Fein gave a cautious reply, suggesting three-way talks with the McAliskey family and the SDLP.
Molloy, who called for the prisoner's immediate release, said her decision would boost the prospects of Sinn Fein's senior strategist, Martin McGuinness, winning the seat.
"The news clears the way for Martin McGuinness, who is head and shoulders above those now contesting the election, to win the seat and properly represent the people of Mid-Ulster," he said.
The Irish government and human rights groups have criticised McAliskey's detention in a London jail and said she should be bailed pending extradition proceedings.

German authorities want to question her about a bombing last year at a British military base in Osnabrueck. The attack was part of the guerrillas' campaign against Britain's rule over Northern Ireland.
